We are Schrodinger's Team (Navi Mumbai) tackling the "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Our vibe is high-energy space exploration, inspired by our Oggy mascot.

Why Join? We are building a fun, interactive training simulator for kids. We have the core architecture ready; you bring your skills to help launch this prototype fast.
summary:
Schrodinger's Astronaut is an interactive lunar survival game that introduces young audiences to the challenges of exploring and living on the Moon. Players take the role of an astronaut stranded following a mission emergency and independently select a lunar landing location. Their choice influences the terrain, temperature conditions and availability of water ice through a simplified environmental model.

The project uses NASA's High Resolution Topographic Map of the Moon, with actual elevation data imported and processed to inform the game's terrain. NASA's 3D Resources and Scientific Visualization Studio Moon model are also used to create the three-dimensional lunar environment.

Players must manage essential resources, explore their surroundings, collect materials, restore damaged base systems, repair a lunar rover and prepare the return spacecraft for launch. By allowing players to collect water ice at suitable polar locations, the game introduces In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) and demonstrates how local resources could support future lunar missions.

Developed using Python for game logic and object movement, with Godot as the game engine, Schrödinger's Astronaut combines exploration, resource management and problem-solving. Its goal is to make lunar science accessible through an interactive experience that connects real lunar data with simplified mission challenges.
details:
Schrodinger's Astronaut:

Schrodinger's Astronaut is an interactive lunar survival and mission-training game designed to introduce young users to the challenges of lunar exploration through an engaging, playable experience.

The player takes the role of an astronaut stranded on the Moon following a mission emergency. Before beginning, the player can independently select a lunar landing location. This choice influences the gameplay, including the terrain encountered, temperature conditions and the availability of water ice in suitable polar regions. The objective is to survive, explore, manage essential resources, restore damaged equipment, repair a lunar rover and prepare the return spacecraft for launch.

A key technical aspect of the project is its use of NASA resources to construct the lunar environment. Our team used NASA's High Resolution Topographic Map of the Moon, importing and processing its actual elevation data to inform the game's terrain representation. We also used NASA's 3D Resources collection and the Moon 3D model provided through NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio to support the three-dimensional representation of the lunar environment. These resources help ground the game environment in actual lunar topography and NASA-produced visual models.

The game also incorporates location-dependent environmental conditions. Terrain is informed by the processed topographic data, while temperature and water-ice availability are represented through a simplified gameplay model. Players selecting suitable polar landing regions can obtain water ice as a resource. This introduces the concept of In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), demonstrating how locally available resources could support future lunar missions.

The gameplay combines exploration, resource management and equipment repair. Players must monitor essential supplies such as oxygen, water and power, collect limited materials, restore damaged base systems, repair the lunar rover and reach the return spacecraft. They must make decisions about resource allocation and equipment repairs to progress through the mission and achieve a successful return.

The project was developed using Python and Godot. Python is used to implement game logic and the movement of objects, while Godot serves as the game engine in which the interactive environment and gameplay are developed and run.

Rather than simply presenting facts about the Moon, Schrodinger's Astronaut allows players to interact with a lunar environment and experience simplified versions of the decisions involved in astronaut survival, navigation, resource allocation and equipment maintenance. Its location-selection mechanic connects geographical differences with practical mission decisions, making lunar exploration more interactive and understandable.

The project aims to make space science accessible to younger audiences while encouraging an understanding of how terrain, environmental conditions and resource availability influence mission planning. It is being developed as a functional game prototype that demonstrates these concepts through interactive gameplay.
